Part 1 · counting handles

Degrees of freedom (DOF) at steady statestep 1 of 2

Objectives say what to hold. The count of independent handles says how many things can be held at once.

$N_{DOF}$
variables that can be set independently
–
$N_v,\ N_e$
variables; independent equations linking them
–
$$N_{DOF}=N_v-N_e$$
$N_v=7+5+7=19$7 valves, 5 states, 7 flows
$N_e=12$8 balances and relations, 4 outlet valves
$N_{DOF}=19-12=7$equals the 7 valves: one loop each, at most

Interactive · step 2 of 2

Give each handle a job

Pressure, interface and bucket are inventories: each must own a valve that drains it; the weir fixes the inlet level.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Safety comes first; quality is reached through set points, not its own loops.
  • A loop is SP, controller, valve, process and transmitter; the error drives the valve.
  • V-101 has 19 variables and 12 equations: 7 degrees of freedom, 7 valves.
  • Three inventories need loops; the inlet level is fixed by the weir.

Five rules for pairing

Part 1 left seven handles. Now each meets the variable it controls best.

Inventory

the valve that drains it

Direct and fast

one sign, short dead time

Safety apart

own sensors, own valves

Fail safe

gas opens, liquids close

No fighting

loops must not interact

Hand if rare

the choke stays manual

Part 2 · two different questions

Controller action is not valve failure

LoopActionValve failsSafe because
PIC-110directopenrelieves gas
LIC-120directclosedkeeps water seal
LIC-130directclosedkeeps oil seal
TIC-102reverseclosedno heat

Direct: output rises as the measurement rises. Fail position: where the valve goes without air or signal.

Interactive · choose a structure

Beyond a single loop

PIC-111 at 11.0 bar g works as an override: flaring starts only after export cannot hold 10.0.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Each outlet valve controls the inventory it drains.
  • Step tests on the model confirm the pairings; the weir decouples bucket from interface.
  • Action and fail position are chosen separately; gas fails open, liquids closed.
  • Two pressure controllers with separated set points keep flaring the last resort.

Part 3 · the controller

Proportional, integral, derivative (PID)

$e$
error, SP − PV or PV − SP by action
% span
$K_c$
controller gain
%/%
$T_i,\ T_d$
integral (reset) time, derivative time
s
$$\text{OUT}=K_c\left(e+\dfrac{1}{T_i}\int e\,dt-T_d\,\dfrac{d\,\text{PV}}{dt}\right)+\text{bias}$$

Derivative on the measurement; the integral stops at 0 or 100 % (anti-windup).

Interactive · model runs, choke 50 → 60 %

Why P alone is not enough

Self-regulating, P only$e_\infty=\dfrac{\Delta_{load}}{1+K_cK}$
Offset, P only
Offset, PI
0

Doubling $K_c$ roughly halves the offset but never removes it: only the integral term returns PV to SP.

%/%

$t_{28},\ t_{63}$
times to 28.3 % and 63.2 % of the change

%/s per %

Interactive · step 2 of 2 · OUT +5 % in manual

Five loops, two kinds of response

Pressure, temperature and flow settle at a new value; the levels keep ramping — integrating, so they always need a controller.

Part 3 · lambda (IMC) tuning

Choose the speed λ, compute the settings

A step test gave the process. Now we choose how fast the closed loop should be.

$\lambda$
closed-loop time constant you choose
s
Fitted on the previous slide$K,\ \tau,\ \theta$  or  $K',\ \theta$
$$K_c=\dfrac{\tau}{K(\lambda+\theta)},\ T_i=\tau\qquad K_c=\dfrac{2\lambda+\theta}{K'(\lambda+\theta)^2},\ T_i=2\lambda+\theta$$

Left: self-regulating. Right: integrating. λ = τ gives a robust loop; averaging levels take minutes.

Interactive · model runs, choke 50 → 60 %

Faster λ, smaller deviation, busier valve

Halving λ cuts the peak deviation but makes the valve move faster; λ is a choice about what the next unit must absorb.

Interactive · 200 runs on copies of the model

Tuning lab

High gain and short reset overshoot; P only leaves an offset. The simulator's tuning (dashed) is the reference.

Interactive · LIC-120, choke 50 → 60 %

Why the interface loop is tuned slowly

The interface only has to stay between 350 and 800 mm: let it swing, and the hydrocyclones get a smooth water flow.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • P alone leaves an offset that shrinks with gain; the integral removes it.
  • Step tests give $K$, $\tau$, $\theta$ for self-regulating loops and $K'$, $\theta$ for levels.
  • Lambda tuning turns the chosen speed λ into $K_c$ and $T_i$.
  • Faster loops cost valve movement; the interface is tuned for smooth outflow.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Count the degrees of freedom first: seven valves, at most seven loops.

2

Pair each inventory with the valve that drains it.

3

Step-test in manual, fit the response, then tune by choosing λ.

4

Tune for what the next unit must absorb, not only for speed.
